text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm Instax Wide 300 Instant Film Camera (Black) Boy! does this camera remind me of my old Polaroid Square Shooter. This camera is NOTHING like your iPhone camera as it's big, and totally analog except for the film counter on the back. I love it when the motor runs and film comes sliding out - a sound I well remember. I think the hardest thing about using this camera was getting the shoulder strap put on, other than that it's very easy to use. Though it is on the big side, it doesn't weigh much and the view finder and shutter button are pretty much intuitive. I'm left handed so holding it like a right-hander took a little getting used too, but it's not a problem for me. This camera is made for right-handers so those who are very much left-handed might not like the way you have to hold it, and the shutter button is on the right side front. It has flash and you can adjust the light/dark and distance to you subject with minimal effort.

Loading the film was easy, aiming at my subject was easy, the shutter button was easy to depress and everything is/was easy. The close-up adapter looks like there's no way it will attach itself to the lens, but somehow it does. I took one close-up of my dog but the picture didn't turn out very good because she moved away right when I hit the shutter button-but that's typical for her. I haven't taken a "selfie" yet but it seems like it will be easy to do.

The color development of the film is pretty good. I took a wide angle picture of my raised garden beds and I was able to get all of them in the picture and the various green colors were vivid. I also took a picture of the front of our house, and though I had to still walk across the street to our neighbor's driveway to get the entire house in the view finder, the picture turned out nice. Again, the colors were bright and vivid. It got the entire house plus some area on both sides. In the past with my other cameras I would have to get further away or be happy with just most of the house in the picture so it's real nice to get the whole thing with room to spare.

The film is kind of pricey. For a pack of 40 pictures it costs around $34.00. I figured it would be kind of expensive and I hope the price of the film goes down some. This is a comfort camera for those of us who grew up with Polaroids. It may be that since we are living in highly uncertain and stressful times, having a camera like this is a cool blast from the past and may make us just feel better having one like this, plus it takes nice pictures.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm Instax Wide 300 Instant Film Camera (Black)

Canon 2562A002 EF 28-135mm f/3.5-5.6 is USM Standard Zoom Lens for Canon SLR Cameras The Canon 28-135mm f/3.5-5.6 lens with Image Stabilization is a very capable, and more importantly, affordable lens,and is perfect for times when you just want to have one lens on the camera but you also want to have a lot of options with your focal range. While you get the benefits of a slight wide to telephoto range in one handy package, you do lose in light stops as you move through the focal range (the maximum aperture stops down as you move toward the telephoto end of the range). This is where the image stabilization comes in very handy, and allows you to keep hand shake at bay even when you have to compromise on shutter speed to get the correct exposure.

I've had no complaints about the optical quality, I think you'll be pleased with the shots you get from it - the lens may be cheap but don't confuse that with what the quality of image this lens can provide. Keep in mind on a camera with a cropped sensor (any Canon DSLR model other than the 5D and 1D models) the focal range is equivalent to @45-215mm - you lose a bit of the wide angle advantage, but you get more telephoto, so it depends which end of the focal range you value the most as to whether that is a disadvantage or not.
text_fidelity_b: Canon 2562A002 EF 28-135mm f/3.5-5.6 is USM Standard Zoom Lens for Canon SLR Cameras

text_fidelity_a:
Toshiba TransMemory Pro USB 3.0 Flash Drive (PFU064U-1BDS) With its huge 64GB file storage capacity, this flash drive can theoretically store the entire contents of a PC's hard drive and its operating system. Since I don't have that many files to store on an everyday basis, I am reserving this flash drive to store high-resolution videos and other RAM-eating monster files.

For $80, this is rather overpriced. There are USB drives that are cheaper and will do the job just as well. To make the USB look like it's worth the extra price, Toshiba made the casing unnecessarily oversized - there's no practical reason why the USB case had to be so wide (you will have trouble sticking another USB drive next to it, which is annoying). It's a gimmick to impress the user, nothing more. However, when you hold it in your hand, it's not as heavy as the metallic finish would lead you to believe - it's actually very lightweight, and to be honest, feels cheap. I have questions of its durability, despite the fancy advertising.

To test, I copied all the videos I had stored in my PC to see how fast it would be to store all of them on this monster drive. I was disappointed that the saving time was not noticeably faster, which may not be the fault of the USB drive but rather my computer. However, I have to say it was a relief that I never got the "you don't have enough memory" message, so you can count on this USB to store tons of videos you can't find room for elsewhere.

The only drawback to this single-USB method of storage is that I don't feel entirely comfortable saving so much stuff on just ONE drive, despite its capacity. It's equivalent to putting all your eggs in one basket - what if you lose that single USB - you're screwed. Though convenient, I'd rather spread out my back-up files, so if you use this USB to save a huge file, I'd buy more than one just to be safe.

The other thing I thought was unnecessary was the included encryption software that's included on the drive. You only see it when you open up the Files folder, and there are two lengthy PDFs with instructions on how to activate the password and security options. Fortunately you do not require to activate them in order to use the drive - I've never found I needed such security measures, but if you plan to store financial data on this USB, it's a good feature.

Lastly, I hate the fact that, unlike my other drives, it has a cap. I am forever losing the caps to my flash drives and have since opted to buy only the retractable ones, where you can slide the connector in or out. Too bad this one doesn't have it, otherwise I would have added a star.

So, in short, a mixed review. Give me a drive that's cheaper, that's big on the inside but small on the outside, capless, and I'd buy more of them.
text_fidelity_b: Toshiba TransMemory Pro USB 3.0 Flash Drive (PFU064U-1BDS)

Sound quality is clear, but very bass heavy. Unlike more better quality earbuds, these have no equalizer feature to help you get a more natural sound profile. Curiously, these earbuds do have the AAC CODEC for iPhones, but no aptX that Android phones prefer.

Noise cancellation is pretty good for this price range, though it does reduce your battery life somewhat. Battery life without noise cancellation is about average for the budget-price point, but not as good as what more expensive earbuds offer.

There is no wireless charging, though I'm not a huge fan of that anyway, especially for headphones.

I give 5 stars for OnePlus phone owners, but only 3.5 stars for everyone else.

SAMSUNG 75-Inch Class QLED 4K The Frame LS03B Series, Quantum HDR, Art Mode, Anti-Reflection Matte Display, Slim Fit Wall Mount Included, Smart TV w/ Alexa Built-In (QN75LS03BAFXZA, Latest Model) I am using this TV as my primary PC monitor. Since I don't have my PC stationed at a desk but rather use a wireless keyboard and mouse to remotely sit where I want to, the screen can be on my wall and I can comfortably sit back in my La-Z-Boy recliner several feet away while doing work, surfing the web, gaming, or whatever. This screen is really perfect for this, with a 120 hertz rate and 4k graphics. And of course it still maintains all the regular functionality of a TV as well.

I primarily use my computer to illustrate books for my day job, and this screen really makes my illustrations look great! Set to "Graphics" mode (rather than "Entertain" mode) the colors are true and the shadows retain great detail; the highlights are smooth, and clean. The color profile is easy to adjust. I really appreciate all of this very much. In the "Entertain" mode, the colors are amped up and the graphics are sharpened, etc. This is nice for watching films and gaming, but for doing graphics work it's absolutely necessary to have the colors and details represented accurately. The excellent anti-reflection and anti-glare features are also extremely helpful in this regard.

The native speakers are about what you would expect; they aren't amazing, but they aren't really all that bad for what this TV is intended to be either. It's really all about the screen. I personally don't care too much about the speakers, because 95% of the time that I use the screen I'm wearing headphones anyway so that I don't disturb my family. But if you're a real audiophile and that sort of thing is important to you, I would suggest you get some nice speakers to go with the TV, because the built-in speakers are clearly only meant to be just good enough to pass muster, and aren't anything to be wowed by.

For me, it's really nice that it doubles as a picture frame when I'm not actively using it for anything else. I have loaded an assortment of my own favorite photographs and illustrations for it to cycle through, and they look really great on this screen, but you can also access a fairly good assortment of art through the TV itself. This turns what is typically a bit of an eyesore in my opinion (I don't like the intrusive look of too much electronic technology in my home) into a lovely, active decoration instead.

I have not ordered a decorative frame to customize it; the reviews on those seem to indicate that they are perhaps overpriced and fragile, and I think it would be easy enough to make my own anyway, which I plan to do. I think having a frame on it would just be the cherry on top, so to speak.

And to reassure anyone who is wondering about the review that said this is the 2021 model, I think there must have been some confusion on one end or the other, because I definitely received the 2022 model that I ordered.

It came with the "Slim-Fit Wall Mount" included in the box (it's in the Styrofoam packing; I think another reviewer might have just not seen it, as it's not very large and it weighs much less than you might expect) along with a decent length of "One Invisible Connection" cable to attach it to the "One Connect Box" controller. This cable is just silver braid with a clear coating on it to help it blend in better than a regular black plastic cable. It serves as a power source as well as controlling the TV, so there's no bundle of unsightly cables hanging down from the screen.

The connect box replaces the usual bulk of the TV, which is what allows the screen to hang so flat on the wall like a regular picture frame. To use the TV, you'll need to position the One Connect box where you can use the remote to control it. It can be positioned anywhere so long as it's within reach of the cable. You can buy longer "One Invisible Connection" cables if necessary. The one that was included was long enough for my needs.
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG 75-Inch Class QLED 4K The Frame LS03B Series, Quantum HDR, Art Mode, Anti-Reflection Matte Display, Slim Fit Wall Mount Included, Smart TV w/ Alexa Built-In (QN75LS03BAFXZA, Latest Model)

For me, it’s not a worthy replacement. It’s a backup mouse, or one to take traveling with me when I’m worried my favorite mice might get damaged or lost.

I do really like the adjustable angle of the mouse itself. The base allows you to set the mouse at 0 degrees or 20 degrees. That feature drew me to the trackball, and I think it’s implemented well. The mouse is rock steady at 0 or 20 degrees, but it’s easy to switch between the options. And because it’s built in, there are no extra parts to carry or worry about losing. For me, the 20 degree angle feels very natural, and that’s the one thing I miss when I go back to my usual mice.

The trackball itself feels sluggish and inconsistent. I’ve tried adjusting the DPI, but that’s not the problem. Sometimes the ball registers the movement of my thumb and sometimes it doesn’t. I did check the ball and sensors; they are clean. The ball is actually hard to pop out, I needed to stick a pen through the small hole to get it out.

The left and right click are soft and muted sounding. Which is okay, but then the scroll wheel click is loud in comparison. The scroll wheel has some resistance, it’s like scrolling through quicksand.

The mouse charges via USB-C.
text_fidelity_b: ProtoArc Wireless Bluetooth Trackball Mouse, EM01 2.4G RGB Ergonomic Rechargeable Rollerball Mice, 3 Device Connection&Thumb Control, Compatible for PC, iPad, Mac, Windows-White Silver

text_fidelity_a:
Polaroid Cube+ 1440p Mini Lifestyle Action Camera with Wi-Fi & Image Stabilization (Red) [[VIDEOID:c23012732deceb9d78b96d41ac89bfcb]] [[VIDEOID:56e6589f81a80deb1709b51fc87a42ef]] [[VIDEOID:bdf9b77251e219b84bed6372225dbf2a]] [[VIDEOID:838bfc2c03ad2a6d884b05f4a37eddbe]] [[VIDEOID:f7f3bb80516774e2cc828f076249211a]] [[VIDEOID:d48cd1a96b9a119e675001d320845a53]] [[VIDEOID:9363c8a20797fe64545aeb51179ca502]] [[VIDEOID:3371609d21e77efbab0cfd0f6265a782]] This is a terrific little action camera that has remarkable clear video, good audio and is extremely easy to use. I understand there were some problems with audio in the earlier versions, but it seems to be all fixed now because the sound quality was excellent when tested both indoors and outside.

I won't bore you with going over all of the specs which you can read in the product description, but I'll tell you how easy it is to use. Mine arrived partially charged, so I used my fingernail to open the back port and inset the included 8gb micro SD card, then charged it fully within an hour. On a full battery it can operate for about 107 minutes and when depleted it takes between 1.5 to 2 hrs to fully charge.

I downloaded the app to my iPad for free from the app store, then did some testing. It connected easily to my WiFi and the interface understandable and easy to use giving you the choice to shoot still photos or videos in several different resolutions. You can also import the photos or videos taken with the camera to your cell phone, your iPad, or share them using the WiFi connection to import them.

This little camera takes gorgeous high def photos, and the audio inside is crystal clear. When I was offered the opportunity by the manufacturer to test the Cube+ I went ahead and purchased a [[ASIN:B00NXK3JTI Polaroid Helmet Mount for the Polaroid CUBE, CUBE+ HD Action Lifestyle Camera]] so I would be able to properly test it in action in order to determine video and sound quality outside in the elements.

I attached the helmet mount to my 9 y/o granddaughter's helmet, placed the Cube+ in it, started it through the app on my iPad and sent her out on her scooter to see how the video and audio quality was. I've attached a short part of the video here so you can assess it for yourself, but I'm quite pleased with the quality of both the picture and the sound, and I didn't experience any lag time in regards to the app.

It does record video in MP4 format, so if you have trouble hearing the audio on your computer you should download QuickTime Player or VLC Player. Both downloads are free and should allow you to view the files and hear the audio. VLC also has a free converter available in case you prefer to use Windows Media Player or Windows Movie Maker. I use a free app called Trim & Cut on my iPad which shortens, condenses, and converts my videos to the format I prefer, and that's what I used for the video I've attached here.

This is a reasonably priced tough little action camera that's easy to use and produces great quality video. It's weather resistant and splashproof so it can handle the outdoors already, but I plan to buy the waterproof case for it so we can have fun swimming with it on this summer. I don't own a GoPro, so I have nothing to compare this to, but from a user's stand point I can definitely tell you that this is user friendly, easy to operate and does a remarkably good job! Enjoy!

This camera was provided at no cost by the manufacturer for evaluation and review.
text_fidelity_b: Polaroid Cube+ 1440p Mini Lifestyle Action Camera with Wi-Fi & Image Stabilization (Red)

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Fire HD 8.9", Dolby Audio, Dual-Band Wi-Fi, 32 GB (Previous Generation - 2nd) SEE BELOW FOR LATEST ON 5-3-13
SEE BELOW FOR LATEST ON 5-11-13 SECOND DEVICE GOING BACK TOO. SOUND FAILED.
SEE BELOW FOR FINAL REVIEW, ALL POSITIVE, 5-20-13

5-11-13 I REALLY DON'T KNOW HOW TO RATE THIS THING NOW. WHEN IT RUNS IT IS FINE. WHEN IT DOESN'T IT ISN'T. NOW THE SOUND HAS FAILED. CAN'T RUN PANDORA, ANY WEBSITE THAT PLAYS AN AUDIO TRACK WITH VIDEO OR MUSIC; CAN'T RUN MP3 OR MP4 FILES AND HEAR ANY SOUND. ANOTHER BEING SHIPPED TO ARRIVE HERE TUESDAY. I AM GETTING REALLY TIRED OF REBUILDING MY BOOKMARKS, APPS, PREFERENCES, ETC. I HAVE WASTED HOURS AND HOURS DOING THIS NOW. I WAS EVEN SO HAPPY THIS TIME THAT I BOUGHT MY WIFE A 7" FIRE HD FOR MOTHER'S DAY. I PRAY HER'S WORKS. I HAVE ALMOST COMPLETELY LOST MY FAITH IN FIRE HD.

The above, and the stuff I deleted from my first review had to do with screen flaws in the first and dead sound card in second. All cleared up and the cogent review comes next.

5-20-13

PROBLEMS RESOLVED WITH THIRD DEVICE. WHEN THEY WORK AND WITH SOME APPS TO SPEED THINGS UP, IT IS 5 STARS NOW.

While waiting for the 3rd device I checked around the web for quality issues with other vendors and discovered they all have problems now. The race to grab some market share is pushing new/re-designed devices out too fast and DOA and other issues are rampant in the industry. Amazom actually may be a bit better; the offset is that if you have a problem and get on the phone with them it is pretty easy to get a new device sent out for exchange via 2-day air, and you keep the one you have until the new arrives. That is an industry high mark that not all vendors have. So this took a lot of the sting out of flaws. Enough.

The device is beautiful, powerful and in 32 GB size has enough memory for most of us, even the video users or gamers who save lots of bytes.

I made the best change though by installing the Dolphin browser app and ES File Explorer. Doplpin is faster than Silk and more flexible. Also you can organzie folders for bookmarks very easily. ES File Exp is a tool you need. You can find almost everything on your device easily and manage apps and other files. They are both free and in Amazon store.

I use Last Pass and Xmarks to manage passwords and bookmarks on desktop/laptop machines and they both work very well with Dolphin. So I was able to load a lot of bookmarks easily that otherwise would have been typed in laboriously and taken hours.

I use Gmail because that gives me the perfect multi-platform email program.

I am a Latin student and found a couple of very good Latin apps. I also was able to find The Daily Missal Readings and an app with the Liturgy of the Hours, in both Latin and English. Both available in Amazon Store too.

When in range of Wifi I can do anything I need to do and do it well with the Kindle Fire HD 8.9" When operating stand-alone I have Latin-English books/Bibles on the device and the necessary dictionaries to continue translation. Very handy.

The only fault still, and I have complained about this repeatedly to Amazon, you can look up a foreign word from a book in German, Spanish, Portugese, French and Italian dictionaries, plus several Oriental tongues, but Latin is not a choice. You have to go to the web or type the word out into Google Translate, Whitaker's Words or some online program. It seems it would be easy to add the Latin dictionary as an option because several very good digital versions are around and I use two of them on an e-ink 1st generation Kindle device. Fix that Kindle and you get 10 stars!

In short, buy one but if you have trouble, get to them right away. Of course, read the instructions and make sure your complaint is not from lack of knowledge.

My final words on the subject.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire HD 8.9", Dolby Audio, Dual-Band Wi-Fi, 32 GB (Previous Generation - 2nd)

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Oasis E-reader with Leather Charging Cover - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity, Built-In Audible (Previous Generation - 8th) “I wonder how long it has been we readers have gazed at the young person sitting under a tree at night reading a book on the Kindle home screen..oh, our love affair with books and being able to read our stories late into the night…...by candlelight….anywhere.”

Pre-release technology reviewers commenting on the price of the Kindle Oasis are wrong. The new Kindle Oasis is worth the the price Amazon is charging, including cover it hardly represents at all an increase in price when compared with a Kindle Voyage with cover. Yet it provides the two most asked for improvements in mobile devices: increased battery life reducing the need to frequently recharge, and improved screen legibility (new sans-serif Ember font, and more LEDS that provide increased brightness).

“When we are immersed into the story of our favorite books, only that world matters.”

Pre-release technology reviewers have compared the Kindle as a single purpose e-reader, to multipurpose devices like in smartphones, tablets and computers. When we choose to read, we are seeking a bit of solitude in the day and night. Oh, how easy it is to remember being annoyed with yet another incoming phone call, text message or email. The power of focus!

“The tactile feel of a book”

Pre-release technology reviewer have labelled the Kindle as luxurious with it’s leather cover. How soon we forget our books covered with leather! And we are willing to pay an extra price for it!

As I sit across the street from the one and only Amazon retail store “in the world”, I have unboxed and set up my new Kindle Oasis. Maybe I am one of the few ordinary people outside of Amazon and the technology press in the world to have been able to purchase one so soon. The feeling reminds me of going to a release party in the same shopping center for the latest Harry Potter novel.

This Kindle is new, like the latest release from our favorite author.

It connects me to reading anywhere, late at night when there is little light.

The Kindle Oasis is magical.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis E-reader with Leather Charging Cover - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity, Built-In Audible (Previous Generation - 8th)

Tenergy TN480U 8-Bay LCD Display Fast Charger for NiMH/NiCD AA AAA Rechargeable Batteries with 4pcs 2500mah AA and 4pcs 1000mah AAA Rechargeable Batteries The charger comes with 8 AA rechargeable batteries, but not a power supply. Any USB power supply that can provide 1 to 2 amps of current will do. It comes with two cords -- a standard micro USB cord and a type C cord. Either will work to supply power to the charger.

You don't need to charge batteries in pairs with this charger. You can charge any number up to eight at a time. However, the instructions say that a 1 amp power supply is good for charging only up to four batteries, while charging eight requires a 2 amp power supply.

The display is bright and easy to see from even low angles. The display indicates which batteries are still charging, and which are full. The display has a basic progress meter in the form of the number of five bars representing each battery that remain lit as the batteries charge.

As far as the included batteries go, I own several Tenergy batteries already, and they've performed well. I expect these will do the same.

Well, the cotton ball tip of it is thicker than a Q-tip for sure, so cleaning each AirPod compartment in the case is a quicker operation. But is it better? Not really - with a Q-tip I can dip the tip into alcohol and, after cleaning, I throw it away. What do you do with this thing after gunk gets stuck on it? Wash it? If you put it into alcohol to kill germs, you gotta let it dry for a pretty long time - and you still have sterilized gunk on the cotton. So overall, this is not all that clean or convenient.

The set also comes with a sharp pen tip that you use to get earwax out of crevices, I guess - but my AirPods don’t usually have stuff stuck in the AirPods themselves, so that’s not useful to me. The little bristle brush that’s attached to that end is pretty useful for cleaning out dry gunk - but, again, it may get dirty after a few uses. Not hygienic enough for my taste.
Lastly, for the small benefit this might provide to some, it’s another little gadget to get lost within a couple weeks. I always know where my Q-tips are - this thing, not so much.

Cooler Master Hyper 212 EVO V2 CPU Air Cooler with SickleFlow 120, PWM Fan, Direct Contact Technology, 4 Copper Heat Pipes for AMD Ryzen/Intel LGA1700/1200/1151, Silver/Black Boy is this big. Fortunately it fits just barely in my Sentey Gaming case. I had purchased the Arctic Freezer 7 Pro Rev 2 but that was far worse than the AMD 8350's included cooler fan, probably because the contact surface is designed for Intel chips and is much smaller than for AMD chips.
Be prepared for some work installing this fan as you have to install a new back-plate on the motherboard. The included parts are perfect in that they provide everything you will need including the thermal compound. So I also purchased the 2 top case fans (Corsair series). Without the cooler, the top fans did indeed reduce the top CPU temperatures by about 4C degrees - almost as though the case cover is open. With the cooler though the CPU temperature never climbed beyond 61C degrees even when all 8 cores were saturated (was compiling code). Without the cooler and the the top fans I was hitting 70C degrees which is 5 degrees above allowed operating temperature. I am surprised my AMD 8350 is still operational. With the cooler and top fans the temperature drop is 15C which is a win! Maybe I can use the Arcrtic Freezer in an Intel setup.
text_fidelity_b: Cooler Master Hyper 212 EVO V2 CPU Air Cooler with SickleFlow 120, PWM Fan, Direct Contact Technology, 4 Copper Heat Pipes for AMD Ryzen/Intel LGA1700/1200/1151, Silver/Black

Outdoor Tech OT5200 Orcas - Ultra-Light Active Sweat-Proof Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds with Comply Memory Foam Eartips (Black) I live on a farm, so I spend a lot of time outside doing various things. I usually wear a pair of Skullcandy Hesh headphones, but I’m worried that constantly sweating will mean I’ll be replacing them regularly. So I was excited to check out Outdoor Tech’s Orcas, both because they are wireless and because they fit inside the ear. Less sweat all over everything, yay!

Unfortunately, the Orcas were horribly uncomfortable for me. I have small ears, so even the smallest ear tips (there are 3 sizes) were too big. It hurt to have them in for even 5 minutes. I tried them out while doing something that didn’t involve a lot of movement — weeding — and even then they kept falling out of my ears. I had to keep taking my gloves off and forcing them back in my ears. So I can’t imagine how they would stay in for anything more active. The “ear fins” are a neat idea, but again, both pairs are too big for me. I squished them in, but one shake of my head dislodged them.

Another note for the ear fins — if you have any piercings inside your ears, such as a rook or a forward helix, they won’t fit.

I did have trouble pairing the earbuds with my phone, but after tweeting to Outdoor Tech, they set me up with tech support and I had a reply within 10 minutes. (Email is support@outdoortech.com).

The sound quality was okay, nothing super great.

My main issue with the earbuds is just that they’re so uncomfortable! If you have small ears or problems wearing this type of headphones, I’d skip them. I’ll be sticking to my Skullcandys.
text_fidelity_b: Outdoor Tech OT5200 Orcas - Ultra-Light Active Sweat-Proof Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds with Comply Memory Foam Eartips (Black)

The other had a well-established brand name, although I don't actually remember what it was. They are actually pretty similar, with the other having decent instructions, feeling just slightly more solid, and better cable management overall.

They both have to be messed with, tightened, and tweaked to get them to work the way you want them to. Thankfully, I don't need either to be constantly moved, but constant re-positioning will be challenging on either stand. Both of them, you don't have to put a hole in your desk. You also need to be very careful (with both of them) to position your cables with just the right amount of slack so that they don't look stupid, but have enough slack to reposition when necessary without stretching the cables.

I like to use two small TVs to use as monitors and run 2 no-nonsense (i.e., thin) HDMI cables, coax, an audio cable, and the power to each. That way, you can set the desk up to accommodate two different docking stations. Don't forget Ethernet if the TVs are smart (mine are not, but they have PIP). If you really take your time, you can fit all that stuff in, and hopefully never have to re-run cables, because it is sort of a pain (but well worth it). Get black cables to match.

text_fidelity_a: Arlo VMC4030-100NAR PRO Add-on Camera, White (Renewed) I received my Arlo Pro ahead of the delivery schedule. It was packaged nicely/professionally even though it is refurbished & came with charging/mounting accessories. I already have 3 Arlo cameras from before and wanted to add an additional camera and read that the Arlo Pro worked more efficiently than the Arlo 2. I struggled the first night setting it up (otherwise a very fast system to set up). I had placed it in a window which prohibited the motion device, so I ended up mounting it outside (and I do purchase the silicon skins to protect my devices) with the suggestion of Tech support and it works beautifully now (tech support wait time was less than 2 minutes on a Sunday afternoon/PST). At first, the camera appeared to have a glitch with a constant flashing, so I removed the battery and reinserted it and it was fine. Tech support was able to remote into my cameras to test whether it was getting Wifi, optimized settings, signals, etc. which was very helpful in figuring out where I was having my issue. Video is in color; it records sounds excellently; AND has a mic which I haven't accessed yet. All added features can be customized or turned off altogether (i.e., sound). In trying to set up my Pro, I watched a few Arlo videos which introduced me to the "MODE" tab option which then allowed me to access ALL my cameras in customizing my cameras better than just going straight into DEVICE tab. Not confirmed, but I think the MODE overrides any settings that you would do to your device if you go directly into DEVICE tab. Select MODE tab, then select your BASE, then click on your cameras individually & SAVE. Having accessed the MODE, ALL my cameras are now working much better. I get email alerts (which is set under MODE & can be turned off if you wish). I have had my Arlo system since 2016 and with my new addition, can't beat the price and reliability of the device. However, I do clean the lenses periodically for optimum motion detection. I do like that the Arlo Pro is rechargeable because my other 3 are not and it costs me about $40 in batteries every 3 months (those cameras take 4 batteries each).  If you find video you want to save, you can download it to your PC/Smart Phone for safe keeping; otherwise, Arlo Cloud clears your video library on the 7th day (which comes with the camera free with the option to subscribe to Arlo if you want a longer history). Bottom-line, you can purchase this system and grow it to meet your needs and upgrade cameras to which the base will support it. I can access https://arlo.netgear.com/#/login via PC or SmartPhone to view my LIBRARY. I do recommend updating your phone app periodically.
text_fidelity_b: Arlo VMC4030-100NAR PRO Add-on Camera, White (Renewed)

He said it was near impossible with the way the house is built. This was my first time seeing 100 foot long ethernet cable--though, I confess, I never thought of looking for such a thing, or even knew they existed. 

He was able to run this directly from the router upstairs, and behind my living room sofa, down the stairway, alongside the wall and into the little room I have set up as an office and for shipping stuff-I've been sewing and shipping a lot of free masks this year. 

You can hardly tell this wire is even there. The little brackets they send with it, hold against the wall, and it's pulled so there's not much slack. I highly recommend these cables to anyone who likes to keep an old fashion pc, like me...or, you just need the internet in a far off place and need a super long cable.

CyberPower CP685AVRLCD Intelligent LCD UPS System, 685VA/390W, 8 Outlets, AVR, Compact I have two of the larger Cyberpower UPS for my desktop systems and they have performed perfectly for the past (nearly) five years. So, when I needed a UPS for my cable modem and router I picked another Cyberpower. Since the draw on the two attached devices is so low I went with a lower capacity. They have other models that have about the same power output, but this model offers a screen to check load, run time, and other metrics while the unit is running. I've found that screen very helpful on my other UPS' so I went with this model.

Construction quality is very solid. There are 8 outlets - 4 for surge only (and are always on); 4 with surge and battery backup. The battery is replaceable, but I don't expect to have to do that anytime soon - both my other systems are running on their original batteries and still maintain a full charge after nearly 5 years of use.

My cable modem (a Motorola) and router (a Linksys) get about 60 minutes of run time off of the battery, which is more than enough for my needs.

I did not use the included software since I don't have a PC attached, so I can't comment on its features.

Highly recommend for a mid-level UPS system.
text_fidelity_b: CyberPower CP685AVRLCD Intelligent LCD UPS System, 685VA/390W, 8 Outlets, AVR, Compact

Echo Auto (1st gen) - Hands-free Alexa in your car with your phone The Echo Auto is a great item for the car, it simply can't do what you want it to do in the long run. The problems I have had with it are:
1. Cannot change the name of the device. For some reason this is not possible. Even if you wanted to name it "Car" or "Kia" or something logical, you will be unable to do so.
2. Pandora is not your phone's Pandora. Even if you can play music from Pandora via this device, if your phone is modified (like ad blocking) it breaks it's ability to play songs. No easy way to access the radio stations you have pre-configured. Should you not specify a radio station, be prepared to have your genre to be Rap and Hip Hop.
3. Getting it to call or send SMS is frustrating. You have to wait for the beep, then fight over which entry you really wanted. The pre-beep routine is not fluid for this. Its ability to select from the contacts is also compromised.

Overall, it does what it says it does. However, it's implementation of music control and calls/SMS needs much work. Lastly, the case needs a point to be able to hook it on something. I will be honest - I got these to use to connect my new phone (USB-C) to a variety of devices that still use the USB-A ports, like my car, my pc, an old laptop, etc. I have fast chargers, but they all have USB-C ports, and thus these cables would not really work on them.

All my other fast charging cables will give a watt indicator (45W, 60W, 100W) as a charging speed - these cables do not, leaving me to guess. Searching online left me more confused, as there seem to be many different answers to what charging speed QC 3.0 will be, from 18W to 36W to 100W. One or none of these may be right - I really do not know. However, since I am not using these cables for fast charging, it is not very vital information for me.

Nice cables, well built, that function well. Fast charging speed is uncertain.

text_fidelity_a:
ZOMEi Tripod, 65" Camera Tripod for Canon Nikon DSLR, Aluminum Alloy Tripod with 360 Degree Ball Head, Professional Tripod for Travel and Work (Orange) This tripod is advertised as 65 inches tall, but that is misleading since you can only reach that height with the center post full extended and somewhat unstable. Most tripods are measured with just the legs and not including the center post or head. This one is about 50 inches tall or 57 inches with the included ball head. You can compare that measurement to other brands.

For a tripod of this height, this one is relatively lightweight and folds up into a compact 20-inch-long case. That makes it very portable for field use. However, they did have to make a lot of compromises in stability to make it this compact and lightweight. The legs have 4 sections (compared to 2 or 3 sections on sturdier tripods) and the thinnest sections are somewhat flexy under moderate weight or in a moderate wind. I don't trust this tripod with a mid-weight SLR camera and exposures of more than 1 second (unless you have the legs folded to half length). For a lightweight camera and fast exposure, this tripod is fine. However, I still would not trust extending the center post in windy conditions, since that amplifies the instability of the tripod legs.

The tripod is attractively finished. I do not like all the twist locks that are slow to operate (compared to cam-locks) and with 4 leg sections, this tripod has lots of twist-locks.

The ball head works OK for this price level and has a quick release plate that also works OK. This company has several different quick release plates sold separately, hopefully one of those will work with this tripod so you can easily use different cameras on it. I have not tried to figure out which one to buy yet, though.

Other people are complaining about the zipper on the case. The zipper on my case broke on the first day of use, too. Just the zipper pull, which is not too expensive to replace.

In summary, this tripod works OK for this price level if you are using a smaller camera and fast exposures. If their goal was to make a lightweight portable tripod, I wish they had made it sturdier and shorter instead of flimsy and taller.
text_fidelity_b: ZOMEi Tripod, 65" Camera Tripod for Canon Nikon DSLR, Aluminum Alloy Tripod with 360 Degree Ball Head, Professional Tripod for Travel and Work (Orange)

Instead, this backpack has quite a few well-done features, and the overall appearance is very striking.

It’s made mostly of canvas, which gives is a “broken in” look right from the start. It’s a very nice change from the usual nylon packs. The canvas is thick and sturdy, and has a great feel to it.

The build quality is impressive considering the price. The stitching is all tight and even, the zippers are of good quality, and the snaps/fasteners are all solid and durable. The strap padding is a little thin, but still comfortable. I was really pleased to see that there was padding on the back. That’s not an option I was expecting at this price. It gives the pack a much more comfortable feel when it’s loaded down.

The inside is lined with a smooth, snag-free lining that’s either nylon or poly (not 100% sure). In any case, it is also very well stitched, with no loose threads, sags or puckers in the material. It makes it very easy to slide books, laptops, etc. in and out of the pack. There are also a couple of compartments inside the pack, both zippered and open, to help organize all the little items that everyone needs to tote around. Additional pouches are on the outside of the pack, which are great for easy access. I didn't have any problem stowing all my small items inside of some type of pouch.

The size is ample for a typical laptop plus a few other items. I loaded it down with books to see if it could take the weight, and the pack performed very well.

The build quality, looks and performance make this an excellent value for the price. Well worth considering if you’re looking for a pack that won’t break the bank in terms of cost.

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech HD Pro Webcam C920, Widescreen Video Calling and Recording, 1080p Camera, Desktop or Laptop Webcam (Discontinued by manufacturer) I was able to do a direct side-by-side comparison between three Logitech webcams: the C920, C615, and C525. Here is what I found:

Right away I noticed that the C920 was a superior product - as it should be, considering it is Logitech's flagship webcam at the moment. But my initial impression was that the extra features might not be worth the size and setup tradeoff. There are three things that the C920 does not have:

1) While all three models attach to your computer monitor in about the same way and all three can tilt up and down, only the C525 and C615 can turn side to side. In fact, they can turn around 360 degrees and more. The C920, however, has a threaded tripod mount, as does the C615.

2) The C920 lacks the excellent "fold-and-go" design of the other two models, which makes packing and travelling easy, while protecting the lenses. In contrast, the C920 is much larger and stationary.

3) The C615 comes with a shorter USB cable AND an extension for more versatility. The C920 - like the C525 - comes with only a full length cable (~6'). My wish for all three models is that they come with a detachable USB cable, which would make them all much more portable and easy to carry around, especially in this age when most people travel with at least one or two USB cables.

But when I actually sat down to do some serious comparisons, I realized just how much more advanced the C920 is, most notably in its use of H.264 compression and its autofocus feature.

H.264 is a standard being utilized more and more for video of all sorts, and it makes a huge difference here. Having used all three webcams on the same computer and with the same software, the C920 compresses 1080p video completely while recording and takes about 49MB per 1 minute of recording on the highest settings (720p for one minute takes about 31MB). That uses *.mp4 format.

Meanwhile, the C615 and C525 use *.wmv format and take 99MB and 44MB for one minute of video at 1080p and 720p, respectively. The real problem, though, is that you then have to sit and wait for the video to compress if you are working in 1080.

If you're interested, The C920 has 1 zoom level at 1080 and 4 levels at 720. The C615 has 0 zoom levels at 1080 and about 10 at 720. The C525 has about 10 at 720. All can be used during recording, but the quality involved with the C920 is again far superior.

Also, the autofocus is much better on the C920, with less flickering and light change. You can really get up close and show off your pores and beard growth.

In conclusion, the optics and hardware of the C920 are obviously superior to the others, which are already high quality. If I am using the webcam while highly mobile, then I may opt for one of the others - I might even just settle for the C525 because it's a tiny bit smaller than the C615 and I believe you cannot use the C615 to make 1080p video calling, even if your hotel's Internet service could keep up with the data rate. However, if I am using a webcam at a stationary computer, or am really a videophile, then I definitely want the bigger workhorse.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech HD Pro Webcam C920, Widescreen Video Calling and Recording, 1080p Camera, Desktop or Laptop Webcam (Discontinued by manufacturer)

Razer Deathadder Infrared Gaming Mouse Okay, so Razer has a reputation for making products that are of low quality or break prematurely. There may be some truth to that. The "back" button double and triple clicks. I am going to replace the switch.

There is an LED lighted scroll wheel which feels of quality. The sides are a hard smooth plastic. The rest the body is coated with a rubber-like material. There is a lighted Razer logo and I turned off all the LED's.

Even though there is a problem with my mouse I decided to keep it and fix the problem. I have to say that this is probably the most ergonomic, comfortable mouse I have ever used. It has a very high arch and is shaped for a palm grip. I personally don't know if it would be a good gaming mouse ever. The sides are VERY slippery and if you needed a lot of control I don't know if you would have it. Especially if you had to lift off the mouse to readjust, it may slip. In my opinion the Roccat XTD Kone is the best mouse I have ever used. It is very big and heavy and there are grooves for your thumb and outer fingers. It feels more sturdy.

The reason I gave it 3 stars instead of 4, the mouse is always a little warm to the touch and it seems to absorb heat from your hand and get hotter. The Roccat mouse is made from similar materials and always feels cool. I have heard that there are parts of the circuitry that generate more heat than normal. So in summary, I like it for general use. If I was gaming or doing something that requires precision such as graphic design I would use the Roccat Kone XTD.

Edit: follow up- I have owned this mouse now for 3 weeks and I have it next to the Roccat mouse. I should share that I have used the Razer almost exclusively and switched to the Roccat only when I needed to use forward and back buttons (they are hard to reach on Razer). I think the Razer is more comfortable to rest your hand on for long periods at a time. However, it just seems that I have better control of the right click, left click, and forward-back buttons. The DA causes your hand to form an arch, while your hand is more flat with the Roccat. I wonder if your index finger is in a stronger postion with the Roccat; it feels so.
text_fidelity_b: Razer Deathadder Infrared Gaming Mouse

Garmin nüvi 55LM GPS Navigator System with Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions, Preloaded Maps and Speed Limit Displays (Discontinued by Manufacturer The story is not good here... Took this brand new, updated Garmin 55LM on a trip drive around Vermont and New Hampshire last week.
The Bad:
1) WORST: We were taken off a main road onto a loop of several miles (usually dirt) that then took us back to the main road we were originally on. Crazy, senseless driving directions. Had it set on fastest route. This happened several times, not just once. (Sadly, we were unable to find a map of NH & so had to rely on the Garmin.)
2) Had it set to avoid dirt roads - it didn't, often sending us down obscure and unnecessary back roads.
3) The announcement of where to turn is dicey at best. Sometimes it told us before the road, sometimes it made its announcement AT the turn, and sometimes it didn't speak up until AFTER the turn.
4) "Recalculating" is gone. GONE! I always relied on that to let me know if I'd made a mistake and/or to have it acknowledged when I was changing the route on the fly. Maybe there's a way to turn it back on, but I haven't found it yet.
5) No choice that I could find for American male voice - just two females. I LIKE the male voice.
6) It pretty much refused to route us to four-lane highways for short stretches of a few miles, preferring all manner of roundabout back roads and streets with an infinite number of turns, even though the highway would have saved lots of time.

I do like some of the software features that are new since my old one, hence I didn't give it a one star rating. Nice overview of the whole trip. But there are some serious problems here. Maybe this device would be fine in a larger urban area. It wasted LOTS of time and led to terrible aggravation in rural areas, though.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 55LM GPS Navigator System with Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions, Preloaded Maps and Speed Limit Displays (Discontinued by Manufacturer

Zink Polaroid Snap Instant Digital Camera (Pink) with ZINK Zero Ink Printing Technology [[VIDEOID:fab011cbaf4d8ff273fb360a6d075448]] My granddaughter is too young to remember the big bulky Polaroid instant camera, so when I showed her this camera and told her it took instant pictures that she could use as stickers her comment was "AWESOME", and she's dying to get her hands on it. This compact sized 10 megapixel camera offers users the option of printing 2" x 3" photos instantly or adding up to a 32 GB micro SD card in order to store or share images.

The camera is straight forward and simple to use. If you want to take instant photos just load [[ASIN:B00ZSPI3A6 Polaroid 2x3 inch Premium ZINK Photo Paper TWIN PACK (20 Sheets) - Compatible With Polaroid Snap, Z2300, SocialMatic Instant Cameras & Zip Instant Printer]] into the chamber in the back of the camera, remove the magnetic lens cap, and gently press the viewfinder to turn the camera on.

Using the selector wheel at the top left, you can choose to take your photos in color, black & white, or sepia (which is like old time tin type for an antique look). Choose one, and then press the button next to that to select whether you want the photo to have a border or not. You can even press another button on the top to activate a 10 second delay to take selfies, and there's also a "photo booth mode" which takes a series of six quick pictures over the course of 10 seconds that you can set by depressing the shutter for three seconds.

Once you've chosen all of your desired options simply frame your shot in the viewfinder and press the shutter. There's no zoom or available adjustment, the camera automatically focuses and uses flash if needed, and the 2" x 3" print comes out of the side of the camera clear, sharp, and dry to the touch in under a minute. If you have film loaded the camera is going to print photos automatically when you press the shutter, so don't load paper if you prefer to use the micro SD card and not print. The camera has an auto sleep function that will shut it off to save battery power if sufficient times lapses between use, or you can just press the viewfinder back down to shut it off manually.

There are no instructions that comes with the camera, but you can read or print the manual yourself by going to polaroidsnapcamera dot come. You can also find the firmware update there. Be sure to charge the camera fully when you receive it, then insert a Micro SD card and update the firmware before using it. (Available here: http://polaroid.com/products/polaroid-snap-camera) Besides printing paper, you'll definitely want to have a MicroSD card for the camera and a case: [[ASIN:B017A1D6TI Polaroid Neoprene Pouch for The Polaroid Snap Instant Camera (Black)]].

There are several things about this product that could be improved on:
1. No sample printing paper included
2. No picture preview
3. No strap to attach the lens cover to which would help prevent losing it
4. Viewfinder pops open too easily
5. No instruction manual or link mention of the firmware update (or link to it) included with product

Otherwise, the camera is well made and fun to use. I can see where kids would have a lot of fun with this camera, but the photo paper isn't cheap so I may let my granddaughter use some and then just mostly use the Micro SD card. This could also be useful for producing instant photos at special events such as birthday parties, weddings, proms, and for other occasions, and the peel off backing on the photo paper makes it nice for scrap booking.

This instant camera was provided at no cost for my evaluation and review.
text_fidelity_b: Zink Polaroid Snap Instant Digital Camera (Pink) with ZINK Zero Ink Printing Technology

This little beauty runs my 20V ASUS laptop for a full workday of moderate use (office/design/some YouTube because I waste time) with juice left over at the end of the day. When fully charged, my internal laptop battery doesn't even kick in. I love, love, love it!

Shutting down/putting in sleep mode the laptop and letting it charge from the battery for a little while while off seems to help.

It takes a while to fully charge, basically overnight. I usually just plug it in when I get home, and grab it on the go the next morning.

*I got in the habit of working at the local café garden some years ago, and now just *have to* work outside any moment that's not actually raining cats and dogs. Continued the habit in my building's back yard during the pandemic.

UPDATE JANUARY 2023:
The battery is still going strong after 4 and a half years of almost daily use! This is truly the best purchase I ever made on Amazon.

text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link Deco Mesh WiFi System(Deco M5) –Up to 5,500 sq. ft. Whole Home Coverage and 100+ Devices,WiFi Router/Extender Replacement, Anitivirus, 3-pack This review is for the TP-LInk Mesh WiFi M5 system.
—————
Amended April 28, 2020
Now that I’ve been using this for a couple weeks, I am returning to add these units HAVE NOT cured the dead spots that needed more signal strength. Yes, the WiFi signal is present in those areas of my home. However, the signal strength has not improved over what my centrally located router produced on its own. Essentially for my roughly $125, I got a couple stylish WiFi access points. What I DID NOT GET is the improved coverage promoted in the description.
—————
This IS NOT a plug it in and it works system. You need to know at minimum:
—Your current router’s IP address, the user ID for it, and the password. If you haven’t changed them from the default, you have no business installing a network anything, because you put EVERYTHING on your system at high risk for hacking. Why? The problem is that the default user ID and password are the SAME FOR ALL routers of the same brand (every brand router has a published default user id and password).
—You need to know which of several comm protocols your ISP uses.
—You need to know that IF YOU SWAP OUT YOUR ROUTER for one of the units, the others WILL NOT WORK to extend your WiFi network. For that you need to set these up as extenders, with the first being connected to your existing router.
—To set up a network of WiFi extenders, you need to know how to turn your existing router’s WiFi transmission off. Only then can you use these as extenders, satellites, or whatever you know them as.
—You are highly likely to have to update the firmware on each M5 device.
—You should set aside about two to three hours to set up a network of multiple devices.
—If you set these up as extenders, some of the default security features are switched off. You need to be sure these security features are enabled on your router instead.

I found this an unacceptably under-documented product that forces you to comb through the internet for proper setup tips. I loathe their little booklet that is “documentation” since it is a collection of single pages in multiple languages that direct you to the App Store or Google Play for the app that manages setup. That app is underpowered, has little relevant or helpful information.

I’ve been working with and installing systems from early (1990s) mainframes, Apple IIs, Macs, PCs of all flavors, and networks right up to now. Were it not for that experience, I might never have gotten this to work. Once installed, it works fine.

Recommendation: If your current router is older, you’re probably more likely to get better WiFi coverage by purchasing a newer, more current router. Try that first, and if you don't get the coverage you need, add a couple or three of these.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link Deco Mesh WiFi System(Deco M5) –Up to 5,500 sq. ft. Whole Home Coverage and 100+ Devices,WiFi Router/Extender Replacement, Anitivirus, 3-pack

Legrand - Wiremold Cable Management Kit, Cord Organizer and Hider, Concealer, C210S Cord Cover Kit, White I'm sure they do it for shipping purposes and to appeal to homeowners without tools, but I don't like that they give you multiple short pieces instead of fewer long pieces that you could cut down to appropriate size. That just means you need more couplers; each additional coupler decreases the appeal of the final installation.

Honestly, I hate surface mounted conduit. But there are times when it is required, and in those cases better than nothing. I own my home, so of course I put all permanent links properly inside the walls, but even then, there are times when the Cat/RG/other jacks are not directly behind the furniture holding the devices that need the cables. In these cases, I prefer to mount these with screws, and then caulk and paint them into the painted baseboards so they blend in better, although they have made these with tape for truly temporary installations.

There is just one connector for an inside corner and an outside corner (on the x/z axis). And in my opinion, these are the only two you should really need, and you probably need more of them. I am never going vertical up walls with cables; I just go from the jack along the baseboard to behind the furniture...if I need more than that, I'm afraid I need to just stop being lazy and tear down a wall or something.

I get that if you are in an apartment or a rental property, you may need more flexibility with this. But in my opinion, if you can't do a proper wall-mount TV install without surface-mount conduit, then you should just use a TV stand as God intended because this is not enough to make cables acceptable in such an install (although honestly, it is better than nothing).
text_fidelity_b: Legrand - Wiremold Cable Management Kit, Cord Organizer and Hider, Concealer, C210S Cord Cover Kit, White

Clip-Case Universal Ergonomic Tablet Stand (Tripod Kit) and Smartphone Mount for iPhone iPad iPod Galaxy Droid Kindle Nook This is one of those "why didn't I think of it?" type products. At first glance, it seems quite simple - basically a mini tripod with attachments that allow you to mount a tablet or phone. But after working with it for a while, it's clear a lot of thought went into this.

The tripod is well made and sturdy, consisting mainly of metal. The ball joint at the top is controlled by a built-in key that allows you to loosen and tighten it so it stays put. Each leg extends independently, so you can set the tripod so it is tilted upward (for example, to position a tablet so you can watch a movie at your desk). The attachment screw base has a rubber non-slip insert to protect whatever you're attaching against scratches. It includes a lanyard, but you can easily remove it (which I did) if it's not needed.

The tripod is very compact -- folds up to about 4.5 inches long and about 1 inch wide, so it's easy to carry. With the legs fully extended it is just under 9 inches tall. The legs have a thick rubber tip that keep it well balanced and positioned. I was a bit concerned that the legs didn't have locks, but the tension of the pull out extensions was more than adequate to keep the legs extended even when it was loaded down with an 8.9 inch Kindle Fire.

Impressive quality given the price - much better than expected.

You can also use the tripod as a camera tripod since the attachment screw is a standard size. It worked fine with my Panasonic and Canon point and shoots.

But the star of the show is the clip. You attach it to the back of the device case (you could attach it to the device itself, but it's not recommended) using an adhesive pad. The pad is removable, but is not reusable, so you want to give some thought before you stick it to the case. Once attached, it fits into a "smart mount" that, in turn, attaches to the tripod. Sounds kind of complicated, but it's very simple to use. There is an included instruction sheet, but you can pretty much puzzle it out by just looking at it.

The clip and smart mount are plastic, but seem more than sturdy enough for the job. They clip together with an interlocking system that kept my Kindle very solidly positioned while I was using it.

The only negative I see is the adhesive pad. As with any adhesive, you need to clean the point of contact very well (an alcohol pad is included in the box) and let the adhesive cure for 30 min. I think it's a safe bet that some people won't do both those steps, which opens the door to a significant point of failure.

But, provided you read the instructions, this is a very nicely designed and useful product. Highly recommend.
[The manufacturer provided the product for review]
text_fidelity_b: Clip-Case Universal Ergonomic Tablet Stand (Tripod Kit) and Smartphone Mount for iPhone iPad iPod Galaxy Droid Kindle Nook

2. Both units have power switches. While it's annoying to turn them off after each use, at least you can be sure the batteries aren't draining needlessly.

3. USB receiver hides securely on board the mouse so it shouldn't get lost easily.

4. Keyboard is full and not missing any buttons as far as I can tell. The arrow keys are smushed up, so you may not want this if you actually use those a lot. Even so, this is about as small as you can make a full keyboard, and I like compact for this, because generally if I'm using this, I have two computers going at once (other is wired and for the primary dock at the desk).

Also...both look good and feel good. Keyboard has a built in bump in the back where the batteries go. Would love to have rechargeable or even solar powered set up here, but your AAs should last quite a while (and, admittedly, those can be rechargeable).

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White Black Friday sales have brought the Echo Dot to under $30, and that is how I am now buying my second one.

So yes, often times you do need to formulate your requests in a certain way (for instance, try asking Alexa how much time it will take to go to work... I gave up on this...) and enunciate them more clearly if you missed, but in general, this technology is just amazing.
Sometimes I even ask Alexa for information I don't need, just for fun.

I like that they named it Alexa. That's so much better than "Okay Google." It feels like a real person. Who in hell at Google thought it's a good idea to force users to use their company name, and thus remind them that their huge creepy analytics private data gathering network is behind it?

Possible improvements:
* Bring back the matte finish from 1st gen. I shouldn't have to pay more to not have it shiny...
* Listen to the word "stop" when the alarm is ringing. Currently you need to wait until it's not ringing and then say "Alexa, stop."
* Add confirmation and modification prompts to "Add a new event to the calendar." Currently if she misunderstood one word, you have to start all over again.
* Alexa bluntly tells you that she cannot tell you about the events in your calendar on a specific date... C'mon guys...
* Implement the word "Repeat": sometimes you didn't hear or didn't catch the information you were looking for, and currently you have to formulate your request again
* Only gives info about the last Amazon order. She can retrieve more order but you have to be very specific about what they contain.
* I wish Alexa could Google more stuff.
* Choose your own wake up word

I never use Siri on my iPhone, but for some reason it feels very natural to use Alexa, maybe because the device is more "fixed" whereas my phone could be in a backpack, in the other room...

The Killer App is MUSIC. We have an Echo Dot in the bedroom, and my wife just loves to ask Alexa for tunes. We have it linked to Spotify.

Also, I am a software engineer, and I have added some custom features through my own skills. I wish somebody came up with something simple to add your own skills, because this is really useful. For instance, the bus comes in front of my house at the most random times, so I developed a skill that tells me in how many minutes the next buses will come. So much faster than having to check a website on my phone!
text_fidelity_b: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nuvi 1490LMT 5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator with Lifetime Map & Traffic Updates (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This little device came in handy during my recent trip to San Francisco, CA. I connected my Garmin nüvi 1490LMT 5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator to my Toyota and it worked great. Installing and using this little machine is simple and easy. The instructions are easy to follow. I had a great time going to different places in San Francisco using this GPS and it never failed me. If you take a wrong route or direction, no problem, it will re-calculate and give the directions to get back on the right tack and keep driving. It works wonderfully. This has many features to help you get from point A to point B quickly and safely; features such as audible driving directions with text-to-speech (TTS), spoken street names, real-time traffic updates, and Internet connectivity for points-of-interest search, 5-inch resistive touch screen with colorful, animated map graphics and large easy-to-read screens are some of the coolest features. It comes complete with free lifetime map updates and traffic reports. The traffic reports are indicated pictorially using specific colors; red (heavy traffic), green (easy traffic) and yellow (moderate traffic). You do get a 3D junction view and speed limit indicators. If you are driving over the speed limit, the speed limit (e.g. 65 MPH), the display of 65 MPH goes red, if you are below the speed limit, it goes green.

It also offer robust point-of-interest (POI) search, including good category breakdowns, as well as searches that update in real time as you drive, complete with compass directions. When we were in Berkeley, CA, we were in an area which was completely new to us, and we wanted to go to an Indian restaurant and this feature helped us to find the nearest restaurant.

My brother uses GPS-enabled smart-phones and recommended me to go for GPS and I have never regretted buying this little gizmo, this offers good value for money.

Pros
* Big 5-inch screen
* Free lifetime traffic
* Pedestrian/public transit navigation
* Multi-destination routing
* Lane assist

Cons
* We had routing problems in some cases. It did not give the correct straight forward directions in my own home town. Once the satellite communication did not work when we are going to the airport.
* Traffic/lane info is available only in some cities
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nuvi 1490LMT 5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator with Lifetime Map & Traffic Updates (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Philips BT2500B/37 Wireless Portable Speaker I have owned those annoying bluetooth ear pieces that always feel like they're about to fall off - or actually do. And although the sound varies from product to product, it's just not a system I am comfortable with.

This little speaker is simply perfect for my needs. It is 4 inches by 4 inches wide and only 1 inch thick. It has a switch that you slide to the right when you wish to enable the bluetooth, or to the left to turn it off. There is also another small button right beside the switch that you push in to receive or disconnect a call. A silver volume knob is sleekly incorporated in the overal design. The pairing was instant and consistant. No need to type in some code or wait forever for them to find each other. But here's the most important part - I hear my calls clearly and with no drop off or fade.

In all fairness, I only use this in my car and I don't spend ridiculous amounts of time on my phone when I'm driving. I've used other products with useless results. Half of the time I would risk a ticket by just ditching the ear piece and talking on my cell. In this case, I'm able to place it on the seat next to me and converse without any problems. Now that it's passed my tests, I'll be getting some velcro and mounting it to my dash board when I'm driving, and then just popping it in the glove compartment when I'm done.

The unit comes with a USB charger cable and it had a partial charge when I received it. Once it's fully charged and you turn it on, a blue light will blink for about 2 seconds and then go to a solid blue. According to the enclosed instructions, you will know that the battery is low when it blinks red. Couldn't be easier.

Musically speaking, my JBL and Sony are better designed for that purpose. But as a compact, speaker phone - this Phillips is without equal. Hands-free clarity without an annoying piece of plastic hanging over your ear. What more could you ask?
text_fidelity_b: Philips BT2500B/37 Wireless Portable Speaker

text_fidelity_a:
SABRENT Rocket Q 500GB NVMe PCIe M.2 2280 Internal SSD High Performance Solid State Drive R/W 2000/1000MB/s (SB-RKTQ-500) Compared to the Crucial 1TB M2 NVME I reviewed earlier, this Sabrent 512GB model benchmarks a little faster. And it works just fine on a PCI M2 adapter card, which are only a few bucks. (I bought the cheapest one available and it works.)

The NVME still offers much faster R/W speeds than other drives even when used with SATA 1 (as on my workstation). For example, the SSD I was using as my hard disk benchmarks at about 220MB/second. The Sabrent NVME on a PCI card benchmarks at about 1.5GB/second.

This time I experimented to see if I could get Debian Linux distro running on the NVME on my older workstation.

It took a few tries. Getting the OS to boot directly from the NVME was a no-go. Since the NVME is mounted on an adapter card, I had hoped it would trick the system into thinking it was just an ordinary SATA drive and boot from it. But that didn't happen.

So what I did was installed all the Linux OS EXCEPT for the boot folder on the NVME, and put the boot folder on the SSD HDD. So it boots from the SSD but the entire OS is on the NVME and runs from it.

Step one:

The partition manager in the Debian installer didn't want to partition the NVME at first.

So I bailed out of it and used GParted (Gnome disks utility couldn't do this) to "create partition table" and selected msdos as type. That wiped everything and turned the whole drive into unallocated space. From that point the partition manager worked.

Step two:

From the linux bootable USB installer I partitioned the SSD (not the NVME) with a primary partition labeled (to be mounted) as /boot. (You can make this partition most any size from a few GB on up---the boot files don't require a lot of space.) The remaining space I manually labeled as /msc.

I partitioned the NVME so the installer would put everything else on it, starting with / (root). You can simply make the whole NVME / root and the installer will take care of putting everything else on that drive, or you can do what I did and set up size-defined partitions for /home, /usr, and so on.

After installing the system, the installer asks where you want the bootloader GRUB installed. I selected the SSD.

It worked. The SSD does the booting to the NVME, which then runs the OS. And it did improve speed.
text_fidelity_b: SABRENT Rocket Q 500GB NVMe PCIe M.2 2280 Internal SSD High Performance Solid State Drive R/W 2000/1000MB/s (SB-RKTQ-500)

APC Back-UPS Pro 1000VA UPS Battery Backup & Surge Protector (BR1000G) I got this for Christmas and have only been using it for a few days now. I did have a problem with the set-up since there were no step by step instructions and you are left to figure out what goes where. I had omitted attaching the USB/phone jack between my old Windows XP computer and the UPS. I've used UPS's in years past, but they did not require a USB connection to a computer. I found out I had a problem when I was trying to install the software and it stopped loading and gave me a problem message, but no solution. I called the 1-888 number and without any fuss or waiting I got to speak to someone in the tech department who spoke very good English and solved my problem quickly.

I was tempted to deduct one star for the lousy (or total lack of) any instructions on how to connect this to your computer but didn't since the tech help was so good. There was a picture drawing instructing the user to remove the battery and turn it over so the green tape is on top which I managed to do alright. I don't hear any fan noise whatsoever as some others were complaining of. In fact, it's so quiet I can't even tell it's on unless I go and see the 3 LED lights on the top panel.

I tested it out a few minutes ago by turning off the power to the room that my computer is in. I was downstairs in the garage at the fuse box so I don't know if any beep occurred upstairs, but when I got there the computer was running off the UPS. Every 30 seconds I heard 4 beeps from the UPS telling me that it was being used as the power source. I only have my computer, monitor and modem connected to the UPS. I figure I don't need the extra peripheral equipment to stay powered up since it only sucks more energy from my UPS. I didn't wait to see how long the UPS would power my PC but I did sit there for about 3 minutes before I went downstairs and turned the power back on. My computer had a message on the screen saying that it was now being powered by regular current again (or something to that effect).

So far I like this UPS a LOT. There's nothing more frustrating then losing your work if the power goes off for only a couple of seconds. I edit a lot of music and it's not always easy or convenient to save it while I edit it just because of the nature of the program I use. So, I really like the idea of hearing my 4 beeps to let me know I might need to close out and shut down and not lose any work. I don't always have lights on so there may be nothing to tell me there's been a power outage except for the beeps on this UPS. There is a mute mode, but I need to hear the beeps.
text_fidelity_b: APC Back-UPS Pro 1000VA UPS Battery Backup & Surge Protector (BR1000G)

Power Strip with 3 USB, KPSTEK Flat Plug Extension Cord with 2 Widely Spaced Outlets, Desktop Charging Station for Home, Office, Dorm Essentials, Black - KS2312 This is a combination product with a 5 foot extension cord, 2 AC power outlets, and 3 full-sized USB power ports. Compact size is great for travel, since older hotels don't have enough power outlets for modern travelers and the outlets are often hidden behind desks or under beds.

Unfortunately, the USB power ports are pretty weak. You get 2.4A divided among 3 ports, so if you're trying to charge 3 devices, each one gets less than 1A. Modern smartphones and tablets will often fast-charge at 3A, so charging with these ports will be very slow. USB powered laptops can use even more power and will complain about being charged at less than 3A.

I don't like that there is no USB-C charging port and no USB Power Delivery fast charging, which are becoming the standard for smartphones and laptops.

This device is not UL listed for electrical safety. As phone and tablet and laptop batteries get more and more powerful, electrical safety becomes more and more important. Most power strips from US brands are UL listed, so I cannot recommend a product that is not UL listed.
text_fidelity_b: Power Strip with 3 USB, KPSTEK Flat Plug Extension Cord with 2 Widely Spaced Outlets, Desktop Charging Station for Home, Office, Dorm Essentials, Black - KS2312
